resources.string:
Crypt Vault keeps your files in an encrypted vault on this device. Only your password can open it. If you lose the password and the recovery key, the data is gone for good; nobody, including the developer, can get it back.

The app has no account and no server. Nothing leaves the phone except what you back up to your own cloud storage, still encrypted, and what you share or send yourself.

By continuing you accept the terms of service and acknowledge the privacy policy, both available under Settings › About.

If the app crashes, it can send a report (the error, the stack trace and your device model) to the developer\'s own server. Reports never contain file names, titles, tags, notes, vault names or account names. This is off unless you switch it on, and you can change it in Settings at any time.

An encrypted vault for the files and notes that matter, in the open Cryptomator format: open them in any app, back them up to your own cloud, and mail small items in a container only the recipient can open.
Crypt Vault is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. The source code is at https://github.com/piepgrasInfo/cryptvault.

Cryptomator cryptolib (AGPL-3.0) for the vault format; the recovery-key word list and encoding ported from Cryptomator desktop (GPL-3.0); Kotlin, Jetpack Compose and AndroidX (Apache-2.0); Sentry SDK (MIT), used only if you switch crash reports on.
What the app asks the system for, and why. Nothing here is requested at start; each permission is asked for when a feature first needs it.
Used only for the cloud backup targets you connect, for share links you create, and for crash reports if you switched them on. There are no accounts, no analytics and no advertising.
Progress and failure notices for backups and restores. Asked for the first time you start a backup.
Lets the app hide other apps\' floating windows above its own screens, so nothing can be drawn over the password field. Granted automatically; no prompt.

Lets the app show the system fingerprint, face or screen-lock prompt when a vault has biometric unlock switched on. Nothing biometric is stored by the app: the system keeps the templates and only releases a key after it has verified you. Granted automatically; no prompt.
Lets a backup or restore you started keep running with a progress notification when you leave the app. Used for nothing else; automatic backups after changes run quietly without it.

Asked for only when you connect a WebDAV server on your own network, such as a Nextcloud on a NAS at home, and only on Android 17 or newer, where the system otherwise blocks apps from local addresses. Used for that server and nothing else; Crypt Vault never scans the network.

Unlocked vaults appear as a storage location in the system file picker and the Files app, so other apps can open and save files in them. Only the system\'s own file tools may talk to this part of Crypt Vault; files are decrypted on the fly and nothing is written to disk in the clear. Locking a vault removes it from the picker.
What the app does not ask for

No access to your photos, files or storage in general: files come in through the system picker, the photo picker or sharing, one by one, only when you choose them. No camera permission: taking a photo uses the camera app. No location, contacts or microphone.
Six random words from a public list, about 77 bits. Write them down or memorise them; they are not shown again.
Too easy to guess. Try a few unrelated words.
Forgot the password? Use the recovery key
Biometric unlock was reset (new fingerprint enrolled or key lost). Enter the password; you can switch it on again in the vault settings.
There is no recovery key to show right now. Open it from the vault settings.

These 44 words are the only way into “%1$s” if the password is lost. Write them down, in order, and keep the paper where you keep your other important papers. The same words open the vault in Cryptomator on a computer.
Not copied to the clipboard, not shared, not shown again without the password. Anyone with these words can open the vault without the password.
I have written down all 44 words
Enter the 44-word recovery key of “%1$s” and choose a new password. The vault contents stay as they are; the biometric shortcut is switched off.
The words are all valid but the key does not check out. Check the order.
Fingerprint or face (or the device PIN on Android 11+). The password still works, and it is asked again after a new enrolment.
No strong biometrics or screen lock set up on this device.
The 44 words that reset the password. Asks for the password first.
Copied. The clipboard is cleared after 60 seconds.
%1$s: another device wrote this backup. Open the vault\'s backup settings to choose.

Backup copies this vault, still encrypted, to a place you choose: a WebDAV server such as Nextcloud, or a folder on this device or in a cloud app. It runs a few minutes after you change something and whenever you ask. The password never leaves the device; whoever runs the target sees only encrypted files.
A folder on this device or in a cloud app
Forget “%1$s”? Vaults backed up there stop backing up. The files on the target stay where they are.
The target is no longer connected
Automatic backups wait for an unmetered network. “Back up now” always runs.
Stops backing up this vault. Files already on the target stay there.
Switch off backup for this vault? Nothing is deleted from the target.
Another device wrote this backup last. Restore from it, or take over so that this device writes from now on.
Backup is on. The first run has started.
Nextcloud: create an app password under Settings → Security; the URL ends in /remote.php/dav/files/<user>/. Crypt Vault creates a folder “CryptVault” there.
http:// sends the password and your files unencrypted over the network. Use https:// unless this is a test server on your own machine.
A restore creates a new vault on this device; nothing existing is touched. Only the vault\'s own password can open it.
No Crypt Vault backups found at this target.
Back this vault up to the same place from now on (this device becomes the writer)
This server is on your local network. Android needs your permission for that; allow “Local network” for Crypt Vault in the system settings.
The files go into one container that only the passphrase opens. Send the passphrase another way — a message, a call — never in the same mail.
Opens with 7-Zip, WinRAR, PeaZip, Keka, The Unarchiver or iZip — not with Windows Explorer, the macOS Archive Utility or the iOS Files app.
Opens with age or rage (command line), AgePony (iOS/Android) or Mage (Android).
Opens with GnuPG, Kleopatra/Gpg4win, GPG Suite, Thunderbird or Proton Mail.
Too easy to guess for this format; needs strength %1$d of 4, or six words.
The passphrase is never put into the mail. Copy it now; it is not kept after sharing.
Above 15 MB most mail providers refuse the attachment. Share fewer items, or hand the container to a cloud app instead.
Attached: %1$s — an encrypted %2$s container, %3$s.\n%4$s\nThe passphrase comes separately.

Gmail warns recipients about encrypted archives, and strict company mail systems may hold them back. If a mail does not arrive, hand the container to a cloud app and send a link instead. The passphrase always travels another way.
This is not a container Crypt Vault can open (ZIP with AES, age or OpenPGP).
Enter the passphrase you received separately.
That passphrase does not open it.
Unlock a vault first, then open the attachment again.
This container needs more memory to open than this device allows. Ask the sender for a smaller work factor, or open it on a computer.
